This contribution develops a Neo-Gramscian notion of science diplomacy to explain how processes of weaponisation risk undermining the mediation role of scientific research, its capacity to integrate diverse perspectives and values, and, consequently, its ability to mediate between conflicting norms, values and interests.
Drawing on Nicos Poulantzas’s state theory, the article further elaborates the concept of mediation and illuminates the role of national parliaments as an important mediator between academia and civil society, more generally, and the government. The empirical study explores parliamentary deliberations of the UK National Security Bill in the House of Commons and the House of Lords. It shows how the parliamentary scrutiny failed to curb the significant expansion of governmental authority justified in the name of security, with important consequences for how academics engage with other governments as part of science diplomacy. 
The findings shed light on the significance of public policy and domestic political struggles for international politics. In the context of an ongoing crisis of multilateralism, domestic political dynamics have become even more important.

articles_hidden.title: Climate Change and the Socio-Political Foundations of Welfare
articles_hidden.authors: katharina.zimmermann@uni-hamburg.de
articles_hidden.abstract:
As climate change and decarbonization become central sources of political conflict in Europe, welfare states are increasingly invoked as institutions capable of cushioning transition costs, managing distributional conflict, and stabilizing democratic legitimacy. The article identifies three perspectives in which this expectation appears: green-growth approaches expect welfare institutions to secure the social conditions of low-carbon accumulation; social-democratic and labour-oriented approaches seek to renew class compromise through just transition policies; and post-growth or sustainable-welfare approaches ask whether welfare can be reorganized around needs, sufficiency, and planetary boundaries. Despite their differences, all three perspectives rely on a shared assumption: that the welfare state can provide socio-political stability under ecological constraint. This article problematizes this assumption by reconstructing the historical foundations of welfare-state stabilization. It argues that twentieth-century welfare capitalism functioned as a form of socio-political glue: it mediated the tension between capitalist market inequalities and democratic claims to equality by making market dependence bearable, class compromise plausible, and bounded solidarity legitimate. Yet this glue was fossil in character. It depended on sustained growth, fossil-energy regimes with underpriced social and ecological costs, institutionalized labour relations, nationally bounded solidarity, and the externalization of social and ecological costs.
Climate change unsettles each of these stabilizing mechanisms. It strains the growth-dependent balance between commodification and decommodification; reconfigures class compromise by politicizing fossil-dependent forms of production, consumption, status, and deservingness; and destabilizes closure and containment by making externalized costs return materially, politically, and morally. The article therefore argues that climate change should not be understood only as a new generation of social risks to be absorbed by existing welfare institutions. More fundamentally, it challenges the welfare state’s historically established capacity to process risks, conflicts, and legitimacy claims in familiar ways. Rather than presuming which form of “green glue” should replace the fossil compromise, it calls for a more systematic analysis of the democratic conflicts through which competing projects of welfare-state stabilization are negotiated: who should be protected, who should pay, which losses count as legitimate, which ways of life remain publicly recognized, and through which democratic procedures new forms of socio-political glue can be built under ecological constraint.

articles_hidden.title: Why the Left Leans Socialist and the   Right Leans Capitalist: Class, Coalitions and Where the Link Breaks
articles_hidden.authors: Kaushik E
articles_hidden.abstract:
Political labels are often assumed to map neatly onto economic systems: the left is 
expected to favor socialism and the right capitalism. This paper asks why that pattern exists 
and why it breaks down in some countries. It first examines four explanations for the pattern: 
historical origins, class interest, core values, and coalition bundling. It then compares 
cases, including Sweden, China, the United States and India, where party labels and 
economic policy diverge. The paper argues that the link between political stance and 
economic policy is contingent rather than necessary, and that it varies with a party's voter 
base, a country's history, and its state capacity. The findings suggest that left-right labels 
are an unreliable guide to actual economic policy.

articles_hidden.title: KONTINUITAS DAN REKONTEXTUALISASI UJUNGAN GUMELEM: RITUAL, REPERTOAR TUBUH, DAN LEGITIMASI WARISAN BUDAYA PADA 2026
articles_hidden.authors: Dwi Scativana Isnaeni
articles_hidden.abstract: Ujungan merupakan praktik budaya yang berkembang dalam masyarakat agraris di wilayah Gumelem, Kecamatan Susukan, Kabupaten Banjarnegara. Dokumentasi akademik mengenai Ujungan telah berlangsung sekurang-kurangnya sejak 1999 dan berkembang melalui kajian mengenai ritual meminta hujan, pertunjukan, perubahan fungsi, makna filosofis, terminologi budaya, serta iringan gamelan. Artikel ini bertujuan membaca kembali dokumentasi tersebut untuk menjelaskan bagaimana Ujungan mempertahankan unsur-unsur identitas praktik sekaligus mengalami perubahan konteks sosial, performatif, dan kelembagaan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif interpretif melalui analisis dokumen historis dan budaya. Sumber dipilih berdasarkan keterverifikasian identitas bibliografis, keterkaitan langsung dengan Ujungan, lokasi, periode dokumentasi, dan fokus kajian. Gumelem Wetan dan Gumelem Kulon diperlakukan sebagai lokasi yang berbeda, sedangkan Ujungan di Pelana, Banyumas, dan Kasepuhan Cibadak digunakan sebagai pembanding regional. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa kontinuitas Ujungan tidak terutama terletak pada ketidakberubahan bentuk, melainkan pada keberulangan sejumlah relasi antara ritual, air dan hujan, penggunaan tubuh, aturan pertarungan, otoritas pengendali, musik, dan tindakan sosial setelah konfrontasi. Dokumentasi 1999, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, dan 2026 memperlihatkan bahwa unsur-unsur tersebut bertahan dengan konfigurasi yang tidak selalu sama. Penetapan Ujungan sebagai Warisan Budaya Takbenda Indonesia pada 2026 menambahkan konteks legitimasi kelembagaan, tetapi tidak dapat diperlakukan sebagai bukti otomatis keberlanjutan. Artikel ini mengusulkan konsep kontinuitas berlapis melalui rekontextualisasi untuk memahami Ujungan sebagai praktik ritual-performatif yang dapat berubah tanpa kehilangan seluruh hubungan dengan sejarah, komunitas, dan pengetahuan tubuh yang menopangnya.

articles_hidden.title: Does Crop Diversification Improve Rural Household Income in Bangladesh?
articles_hidden.authors: Imran Hossain
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper examines whether crop diversification improves household income among rural farming households in Bangladesh, using data from the Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES) 2022. Using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with division fixed effects and robust standard errors, the study finds that diversification has a strong and stable positive effect on crop sales income, but not on total household income once household characteristics are controlled. This suggests that diversification operates primarily through the agricultural income channel. The findings carry practical implications for agricultural extension policy in Bangladesh.

articles_hidden.title: Agreement under abstention: an agreement–abstention–conflict triple and sharp bounds for Fleiss' kappa
articles_hidden.authors: Maikel Yelandi Leyva Vázquez; Alexis Matheu Pérez; Bastián Gutiérrez Vargas
articles_hidden.abstract: Raters in agreement studies are often allowed to abstain, for example by answering "can't tell" or "unsure". Abstentions are usually deleted or recoded, and each treatment carries an untested assumption about why raters abstained. We show how to report Fleiss' kappa without such an assumption. Assigning the abstentions to categories changes both the observed agreement and the category totals that determine chance agreement, so the extremes of kappa require optimising the two jointly. A dynamic programme gives the exact extremes over all such completions for two or three categories, with completions that attain and thereby certify them; closed-form bounds enclose them for more categories. A budget interval and tipping points grade conclusions by how far the missing ratings must depart from a reference predictive model. The shares of agreeing, abstaining and conflicting rater pairs, (pA, pU, pC), serve as an intuitive summary. Under independent sampling of units the sample extremes converge to the population identified set, and an exploratory unit bootstrap supports a three-outcome decision: adequate, inadequate or undetermined. In simulations at 2–10% abstention, estimator errors depended on the mechanism; the budget interval contained the complete-data kappa in 97–100% of replicates under random abstention but 44–51% under value-dependent abstention, and population decisions were undetermined in 43–76% of replicates. In crowdsourced weather-sentiment labels, listwise deletion declared agreement adequate where the three-outcome decision was undetermined; in safety ratings of chatbot conversations, listwise estimates fell on both sides of the interval.

articles_hidden.title: Urban Typology is Not Destiny: The High-Modernist Tower and Slab as a Global Outlier in Singapore
articles_hidden.authors: Reuben Xianwei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract:
In global architectural literature, the mid-century high-modernist tower-and-slab block is widely pathologized as a failure of top-down social engineering. Anti-modernist critics routinely embrace architectural determinism, blaming concrete geometry for social decay. This paper challenges that consensus by examining Singapore, where high-modernist public housing constructed by the Housing & Development Board (HDB) shelters over 80 percent of citizens in safe, equity-building estates. Building on Katherine Bristol’s critique of the "Pruitt-Igoe myth," I demonstrate that building typology possesses marginal agency; the global demise of the high-rise slab resulted from welfare state retrenchment, fiscal starvation, and municipal abandonment. In Singapore, the typology succeeded due to a unique political-economic triad: radical land nationalization, captive domestic capital, and sovereign geographical enclosure.

I adopt an object-oriented ontology and James Scott's notion of metis to argue the built form not as an empty vessel but being instrumental constructs that whose users will always develop new Métis and practical knowledges on how to maximise the utility of an urban form. I exemplify the Singaporean architects adapted the slab through vernacular inventions like the open-air "void deck." Ultimately, typology is not destiny but should be understood instrumentally.

articles_hidden.title: The EU’s Biotech Industrial Policy: Between Competitiveness and Geoeconomics
articles_hidden.authors: Jaša Veselinovič
articles_hidden.abstract: This contribution examines the European Union’s emerging biotechnology industrial policy in the context of intensifying US–China technological rivalry, focusing on the relationship between competitiveness, strategic autonomy, and corporate power. The proposed EU Biotech Act seeks to strengthen the sector through regulatory simplification, public financing, strategic projects, and enhanced intellectual property protection. However, its competitiveness-oriented approach obscures the geopolitical and distributional implications of biotechnology policy. The EU’s reluctance to localise production or restrict global interdependencies is driven by the integration of European pharmaceutical multinationals into global value chains and their dependence on US markets and Chinese biotechnology ecosystem. Consequently, strategic autonomy tends to be framed as synonymous with the global profitability of pharmaceutical corporations rather than broader societal resilience. By situating the Biotech Act within debates on intellectual monopoly capitalism, this short reflection questions whether extending intellectual property rights and reducing regulatory barriers will reinforce an increasingly extractive pharmaceutical business model. It ultimately calls for reconsidering the social purpose of EU industrial policy and whether biotechnology sovereignty should prioritise corporate competitiveness or pharmaceuticals as a public good.

articles_hidden.title: Standpoint Theory and the Enactment of the Social Relation of Comradeship through Social Research
articles_hidden.authors: Ioana Cerasella Chis
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper discusses the ethico-political impetus for seeking to establish the social relation of comradeship with socially marginalised research participants of projects concerned with social justice and countering structural oppression. To this end, the paper explores Olufemi O. Táíwò’s (2020) distinction between liberal and constructive approaches to Standpoint Theory, before considering the social relations of allyship and comradeship through the context of a project that examined structural disablement and precarious work in the UK. In light of this analysis, I call on other social researchers to consider the necessity of enacting the social relation of comradeship with socially marginalised participants as a way of affirming mutual recognition, strengthening emancipatory research, and producing socially useful dialogic knowledge.

articles_hidden.title: Developing and Evaluating UTAUT-Informed YouTube-Based Lessons for Grade 11 Oral Communication During Emergency Remote Teaching
articles_hidden.authors: Jo Michael Llamelo
articles_hidden.abstract: This study reports the development and evaluation of YouTube-based lessons for Grade 11 Oral Communication at a private senior high school in the Philippines during emergency remote teaching in Academic Year 2020–2021. As part of my master’s thesis, I analyzed a UTAUT-informed survey of 26 students' attitudes toward YouTube through frequency-based thematic coding and translated its conclusions into nine lesson features, each assigned a theoretical basis in the affective filter hypothesis, the principles of multimedia learning, or the multimedia cone of abstraction. The resulting lessons combined a course-specific YouTube channel, short videos arranged in topic playlists, teacher narration with humor and familiar references, asynchronous access without mandatory downloading or live streaming, and supporting modules. Three expert jurors and 13 student users rated the lessons with instruments adapted from the Department of Education's rating sheet for non-print learning resources. Jurors (M = 4.63) and students (M = 4.62) rated the lessons favorably on a five-point scale, and their comments pointed to refinements in audio consistency, on-screen text, pacing, and technical smoothness. A later reanalysis of the same survey supports most features but shows that some parameters rested on designer judgment and that the supplementary role of the lessons and the cost of access were not carried into design. The study provides a transparent account of how students’ attitudes toward YouTube were translated into lesson features and how the resulting lessons were received.

articles_hidden.title: Making Place for Health and Good Life: Tourism at the Intersection of Philosophy and Public Health
articles_hidden.authors: Fulvio Longato; Patrick Rina; Christian Josef Wiedermann
articles_hidden.abstract: Tourism is increasingly promoted as a resource for health, and destinations market the well-being their landscapes are said to afford; yet the notion of well-being invoked where tourism and public health meet requires further specification, as the fields that converge there do not necessarily use the term in the same sense. The conceptual analysis clarifies well-being by distinguishing its psychological dimensions from its philosophical characterisation in terms of human flourishing, and frames health from a salutogenic perspective. Human flourishing and salutogenesis intersect particularly through meaningfulness and the ways persons engage with what places make possible. Drawing on the phenomenology of the tourist experience and on the literatures of therapeutic landscapes and restorative environments, the paper argues that places contribute to health through multiple and potentially interacting pathways involving characteristics of settings, activities and experiences, and their social and environmental contexts. Embodied pathways further show the interconnection of experiential and bodily dimensions of health. The paper draws out implications for public health and participatory destination design. Alpine tourism destinations provide a suitable context in which these relationships can be examined empirically.

articles_hidden.title: Remembering without institutions: legal-political memory, oral transmission, and diaspora identity among Kurds in Turkey and Europe
articles_hidden.authors: Ramazan BOZTEPE
articles_hidden.abstract: Drawing on 80 interviews across three sub-samples — the Kurdish-majority region of Turkey (n=25), Central Anatolia (n=25), and the European diaspora (n=30) — this article examines how legal-political memory of forced displacement is transmitted across generations. Using an inductively developed 11-category thematic coding framework, we find a sharp geographic gradient in informal oral transmission (64% Region, 40% Central Anatolia, 16.7% diaspora), with an inverse rise in institutional/archival memory in the diaspora (50%, versus 16–20% in Turkey; suggestive rather than conclusive once corrected for multiple comparisons). Spatial displacement is narrated concretely in the region of origin but gives way, in the diaspora, to an abstract negotiation of layered belonging. We suggest that memory transmission without institutional archives relies on embodied domestic channels vulnerable to migration's ruptures — a vulnerability diaspora communities compensate for through new institutional infrastructures rather than reconstruction. The article offers a comparative, exploratory account of how a stateless-nation diaspora reconstructs continuity across ruptured contexts.

articles_hidden.title: Domestic and Family Violence Training Programs for Primary Healthcare Workforces: A Scoping Review
articles_hidden.authors: Bibek Chauhan; Shauna Fjaagesund; Amy Homes; Katrina Andrews; Gregory Nash; Chrystie Myketiak; Kylie Roberson; Sara Richards; Florin Oprescu
articles_hidden.abstract:
Purpose
Domestic and family violence (DFV) is prevalent, and primary healthcare professionals may be well placed to identify and support victim-survivors; however, limited training and organizational support can constrain safe responses. This review mapped DFV training programs for primary healthcare workforces, including targeted groups, content, delivery, and evaluation.
Methods 
A scoping review was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and reported according to PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the characteristics, implementation, or outcomes of DFV workforce training in primary healthcare. Of 1,262 records identified, 16 studies met the inclusion criteria.
Results 
Training most often targeted general practitioners (n = 11) and nurses or midwives (n = 9); administrative staff (n = 4) and practice managers (n = 3) were less frequently included. Common content included DFV identification and inquiry, disclosure response, referral, risk assessment, and safety planning. Face-to-face workshops predominated, often supplemented by mentoring, case discussion, role-play, and implementation support. Evaluations mainly assessed short-term knowledge, confidence, and preparedness; sustained practice and organizational outcomes were assessed less often.
Conclusions 
DFV training may improve primary healthcare professionals’ knowledge, confidence, and preparedness to support victim-survivors, but predominantly short-term and self-reported outcomes limit conclusions about sustained clinical change. Evidence gaps remain in organizational readiness, workforce agency, long-term implementation, and inclusion of non-clinical staff.

articles_hidden.title: Sobre el Estado de Naturaleza como un uso meta teórico en el derecho y la política: excesos y tensiones
articles_hidden.authors: Ángel Gutiérrez Escobedo
articles_hidden.abstract: La relación entre Derecho y Política se disuelve cuando, desde la teoría de la primera, se confunden sus respectivas autonomías operativas con las descripciones propias de una distinción que se excluye a sí misma de lo observado. Durante la presente investigación, se argumentará en contra del principio teórico que sustenta dicha confusión, porque la separación entre Estado de Naturaleza, Sociedad o Legalidad/violencia, son puntos de apoyo insostenibles para sustentar teóricamente el problema de la nomo-génesis. Identificamos el origen de dicha paradoja, a saber, ¿por qué existen las leyes?, en la traducción contemporánea de distintas tesis contractualistas pues el planteamiento original encontraba fortaleza en concepciones sustancialistas ya contradictorias para el presente. Sugerimos, reconfigurar dicho punto de partida para propiciar nuevas perspectivas del derecho que no aseguren su preferencia o necesidad desde la amenaza del Sin-Derecho.

articles_hidden.title: Policy, Procedure, and Public Trust in the Bureaucracy
articles_hidden.authors: Alexander Love; Alexander Sahn
articles_hidden.abstract: Bureaucracies derive their legitimacy from a perception of impartiality, but in polarized societies preferences over outcomes may trump faith in procedure. We study citizens’ evaluations of the policymaking process as a joint function of individual beliefs that bureaucratic procedure was followed and preferences over outcomes. We recontacted and surveyed individuals who recently commented on rules proposed by American federal agencies; in the survey, we embedded two experiments in which individually tailored treatments successfully manipulated beliefs about procedural thoroughness and knowledge of policy outcomes. We find no effects of procedural knowledge but a strong polarizing effect of outcome knowledge: commenters whose preferred outcome was congruent (incongruent) with the agency's action symmetrically increased (decreased) their perceptions of rule legitimacy, attitudes toward notice-and-comment, and agency trust. These findings cast doubt on a major purported benefit of an otherwise costly administrative practice.

articles_hidden.title: Automated Essay Scoring with GPT Models: A Comparison with Human Ratings of IEP Written Products
articles_hidden.authors: Daniel Murcia
articles_hidden.abstract:
This study explores the integration of Large Language Model (LLM)-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) into classroom writing assessment within an Intensive English Program (IEP). Using a corpus of 46 multi-draft capstone essays written by international students in an Academic Literacies course, the study evaluates the performance of two OpenAI models (GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-5.1) against rubric-based human instructor scores. Essays were scored twice by each model under controlled temperature settings to evaluate linear association, systematic bias, inter-model consistency, and performance-band agreement. Findings reveal that while both LLM scores maintain moderate positive correlations with human ratings (r = .44 for GPT-4.1-mini; r = .49 for GPT-5.1), both models exhibit systematic negative bias, scoring essays an average of 13 points lower than the human instructor. However, the two models demonstrate strong inter-model consistency (r = .84) and an exact band-level agreement of 87%. Qualitative analysis of the holistic comments shows that LLMs focus on global discourse features but lack sensitivity to local, process-oriented classroom constructs. The results suggest that uncalibrated zero-shot LLMs serve better as formative diagnostic tools than autonomous grading systems.

Keywords: Automated essay scoring, Large Language Models, GPT-5, L2 academic writing, multi-method validity, formative assessment.

articles_hidden.title: Globalization Unravelling? ASML and the Geopolitics of Europe-China Tech Decoupling
articles_hidden.authors: Naná de Graaff; Jaša Veselinovič; A.G. Tyler
articles_hidden.abstract: This article investigates the geopolitical dynamics driving Europe’s emerging technological decoupling from China. Focusing on the semiconductor industry and the Dutch semiconductor firm ASML, it examines how technonationalism emanating from the US has shaped a small European member state’s policy response amid intensifying US-China rivalry. The article analyses how national security arguments and US strategic influence aimed at undermining China’s advances in high-tech has reshaped the Dutch semiconductor export control regime in a way that seemingly contradicts both ASML’s corporate interests and Dutch long-term economic interests. Moreover, cutting the dependency ties of China to one of the few chokepoint industries and tech firms in the EU arguably undermines its commitment to ‘technological sovereignty’. We explain these puzzling outcomes through the inherent contradictions within technonationalism and the tensions between state and corporate actors strategizing around different national security and profit-oriented interests. As such, we argue that the case of ASML offers a useful prism through which to study the ongoing ‘geoeconomic’ shift in the global political economy in which the alignment of the geopolitical and capital logics characteristic of neoliberal globalisation is coming apart, with state and corporate actors attempting to realign these logics into different configurations.

articles_hidden.title: Decolonising Water Diplomacy: Concepts, Debates, and Practice
articles_hidden.authors: Mohsen Nagheeby
articles_hidden.abstract: Water diplomacy is commonly presented as a practical response to tensions over shared waters. It brings together negotiation, technical expertise, international water law, basin institutions, and practices of cooperation and peacebuilding. Yet the terms through which water diplomacy is often organised — security, cooperation, neutrality, development, expertise, and peace — are not politically innocent. They are shaped by histories of empire, unequal treaties, colonial borders, geopolitical asymmetries, donor agendas, and knowledge hierarchies. This article introduces decolonising water diplomacy as an emerging orientation that does not reject diplomacy, law, science, or cooperation, but asks how their assumptions, procedures, and outcomes are historically produced. It defines water diplomacy, situates it in relation to water security, water peace, critical hydropolitics, water justice, and decolonial thought, and explains what a decolonial perspective adds in practice. The article argues that decolonising water diplomacy does not simply add justice to existing approaches; it asks how peace, security, and cooperation are defined, whose histories and knowledges they privilege, and how they might be reworked toward historical responsibility, epistemic justice, recognition, dignity, and more accountable forms of peace.

articles_hidden.title: Buying Books, Buying Diversity? Public Procurement Theory and the Brazilian State as Book Buyer
articles_hidden.authors: Marcel Felipe Machado Lopes; Paula Roméro Cajaty Lopes
articles_hidden.abstract:
Governments are among the largest single buyers of books, yet public procurement research rarely asks what state purchasing does to the diversity of the market it buys from. This article examines federal book procurement in Brazil using item-level electronic invoice (NF-e) data published by the Office of the Comptroller General (CGU). The data cover 60 months between October 2021 and September 2026 and R$21.9 billion in purchases, 96.7% of which were made by a single buyer, the National Fund for Education Development (FNDE). Drawing on Stirling's variety–balance–disparity framework, we build five indicators of bibliodiversity: supplier concentration (Herfindahl–Hirschman index), the share of the four and eight largest suppliers, supplier evenness, title evenness, and territorial inequality among suppliers.
The results describe a market with high variety but low balance. A median of 280 suppliers invoice the federal government each month, yet the four largest take a median 68% of value, and two publishers, FTD and Moderna, account for 45% of the whole series. Concentration is episodic rather than trending: 13 of 60 months exceed the HHI threshold of 2,500, with no significant monotonic trend. Territorial inequality is extreme and stable (median Gini 0.93), with São Paulo-based emitters taking 93% of value. Title diversity falls when supplier concentration rises (Spearman ρ = −0.61) and has declined sharply since mid-2025.
We read these patterns against transaction cost, principal–agent, competition, strategic-procurement and institutional theories. We argue that, in markets for unique cultural goods purchased without price competition, the locus of competition moves from the tender to the pre-selection stage, so programme design rather than tendering rules becomes the main lever for diversity. We derive five propositions and discuss the data-quality limits of invoice-based procurement analytics.

articles_hidden.title: Social Prescribing and community activities for people living with chronic pain: A Realist Synthesis
articles_hidden.authors: Leila Heelas; Daisy Fancourt; Karen Barker; Alexandra Bradbury; Ann Livingstone; Alexandra Burton
articles_hidden.abstract:
Chronic pain is associated with significant physical and mental health burden to individuals and society. Social determinants of health are associated with an increased prevalence of chronic pain and disability. Social prescribing is an intervention designed to address social determinants of health; however, little is known about how social prescribing can support people living with chronic pain (PECP).
To investigate the mechanisms and contexts by which participation in social prescribing and/or community activities lead to health and wellbeing outcomes in PECP.
A realist synthesis was conducted in November 2024 and updated in March 2026. Context-mechanism-outcome configurations (CMOCs) were produced and mapped to the Multi-Level Mechanisms of Leisure Framework to identify potential psychological, biological, social and behavioural mechanisms.  A programme theory was developed to illustrate how and why social prescribing interventions lead to health and wellbeing outcomes in PECP. 
Of 9761 studies, 35 were included. Four sources explored social prescribing link worker models and thirty-one investigated individual community activities. 15 overarching CMOCs were identified including seven psychological, three biological, three social and two behavioural mechanisms. The CMOCs highlight how creative, cultural and leisure activities, social prescribing pathways and volunteering, lead to intended and unintended outcomes (such as pain resulting in reduced participation in volunteering). This synthesis provides evidence for how social prescribing interventions lead to improved health and wellbeing in PECP and can be used to inform non-clinical service provision, especially where access to pain services is limited.

articles_hidden.title: Unionization in Higher Education: An Industry-Level View
articles_hidden.authors: Joseph van der Naald
articles_hidden.abstract: This research note presents estimates of union membership and collective bargaining coverage in the higher education industry using data from the Current Population Survey. The paper analyzes the extent of union membership and collective bargaining coverage from 1983-2025, both in the industry and among faculty specifically, and estimates of the variation in union membership by employment sector, race and gender for 2024. Using a 10-year span of data, the paper also estimates union wage premiums in the industry and among faculty. This note finds union membership and bargaining coverage has remained stable over the past four decades, but documents notable gendered and ethnoracial disparities in both measures in 2024. Faculty and industry collective bargaining results in earnings premiums ranging between 4% and 5%. The findings present quantitative estimates of unionism and its material effects for higher education workers that complement recent research published by the National Center for the Study of Collective Bargaining in Higher Education and the Professions.

articles_hidden.title: Compensatory Input Versus Unequal Gains: Why Schooling Does Not Necessarily Equalize Socioeconomic Achievement Gaps
articles_hidden.authors: Jan Skopek
articles_hidden.abstract: Recent research has failed to provide clear-cut evidence that schooling equalizes social gaps in achievement. This stands at odds with the dominant view of compensatory input, which holds that even unequal schooling equalizes learning because it compensates for the even more unequal learning inputs children would receive in its absence. I test the previously neglected mechanism of unequal gains from schooling, which could counteract compensatory input and thus explain why studies often fail to find equalization. The unequal gains hypothesis posits a Matthew effect whereby learning gains from schooling depend on children’s prior skills, so that students from higher (lower) socioeconomic backgrounds benefit more (less) from schooling because of their, on average, higher (lower) skills at school entry. Because both mechanisms can operate simultaneously, assessing the equalizing power of schooling requires accounting for achievement prior to schooling. Using data from the newborn cohort of the German National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), I first replicated earlier findings from Germany on the beneficial but non-equalizing effects of school exposure on student achievement—scientific literacy and vocabulary—in Grade 1. Second, after accounting for children’s achievement before schooling, I found evidence of unequal gains counteracting equalization; net of these unequal gains, school exposure did level out learning gaps by social background, although only in the domain of scientific literacy. The findings underline the importance of incorporating prior achievement into studies of school equalization.

articles_hidden.title: Modeling Cooperation as Information Flow: Ripple Structures and Behavioral Digital Twins
articles_hidden.authors: kazutaka hayashi
articles_hidden.abstract:
Recent advances in articial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models, have
signicantly improved performance in language understanding, vision, and reasoning. How-
ever, a fundamental limitation remains: current AI systems still lack an explicit under-
standing of the logical structure by which humans make decisions within specic situations
and relationships. This limitation is not merely a shortage of intelligence, but a missing
layer of context-dependent decision logic. This study proposes a theoretical framework and
methodological protocol that redenes human cooperation as an observable information ow
rather than a psychological or moral phenomenon. We model cooperative propagation as
Ripple structures, which are directional causal chains of actions in which A helps B and B in
turn helps C, and we introduce the concept of a Behavioral Digital Twin, dened as a map-
ping of decision logic derived from situation, relationships, and action history. We further
present a non-interventional observational protocol for capturing naturally occurring coop-
erative behaviors through naturalistic observation environments, and outline a validation
framework for future empirical work. All behavioral events remain voluntary; the proto-
col introduces observation infrastructure without prescribing or incentivizing actions. All
gures and examples in this manuscript are conceptual illustrations intended to clarify the-
oretical constructs. This work aims to provide a foundational layer connecting AI research,
social systems research, and Web3 governance.

articles_hidden.title: Flourishing and Health in Kenya. Philosophical Perspectives and Empirical Insights.
articles_hidden.authors: Maike Ritzer; Steffen Flessa
articles_hidden.abstract: Numerous studies have demonstrated positive associations between broader dimensions of wellbeing and health. However, evidence from Kenya on this association is scarce and mostly focused on broad evaluative measures of wellbeing, such as life satisfaction. This study draws on conceptualizations of wellbeing from Sub-Saharan African philosophical literature as motivation for examining various specific dimensions of wellbeing in the Global Flourishing Study and analyzing their association with subsequent health in Kenya as a case study, using a longitudinal panel design. Data were drawn from waves 1 (2023; n=11389 individuals) and 2 (2024; n= 7698 individuals) of the Global Flourishing Study. The data are representative of the general population in Kenya. Linear regression models with a lagged dependent variable are used to test the association of wave 1 wellbeing indicators with subsequent physical and mental health at wave 2. The findings indicate that several dimensions of wellbeing - including livelihood security, satisfaction with personal relationships, meaning and purpose, agency and freedom to pursue what is most important in life - are positively associated with subsequent self-rated physical and mental health in Kenya.

articles_hidden.title: The Impact of U.S. Tariffs on European Public Opinion: Evidence From a Natural Experiment
articles_hidden.authors: Joseph Noonan
articles_hidden.abstract: How do tariff escalations shape public attitudes in targeted countries? This registered report examines how the second Trump Administration's April 2025 tariff escalation affected European public opinion. Leveraging the announcement's timing during the fieldwork of Standard Eurobarometer 103.3 as an unexpected event, I compare respondents interviewed before and after. Drawing on theories of external threat, in-group identity, and cooperative reciprocity, I test whether the escalation strengthened pro-EU sentiment, worsened views of the United States, and shifted cooperation preferences. I find that it reduced favorable views of the United States, while effects on EU attachment and cooperation preferences were small and non-significant. The decline in favorable views of the United States is concentrated in the most negative response category, indicating that negative views intensified. These results suggest that economic threats from an ally can sharpen antagonism toward the threatening actor without producing broad in-group consolidation or shifts in trade cooperation preferences.

articles_hidden.title: Accountability Gap Behind Predatory Publishing in Philippine Academia
articles_hidden.authors: Jeconiah Dreisbach
articles_hidden.abstract: The mandate of the Philippines’ Commission on Higher Education ties faculty promotion in state universities and colleges to research publications. This commentary argues that the policy's emphasis on publication volume, unmatched by a corresponding verification mechanism, has created conditions in which predatory journals, conferences, and award bodies can thrive. Rising demand for indexed journal publications has already produced unsolicited offers to acquire legitimate, non-profit university journals, commercializing a system meant to signal quality. The threat extends beyond obviously fraudulent venues: recent evidence of paper mines (Barnett & Byrne, 2026), in which openly available datasets are mass-mined into formulaic, artificial-intelligence-assisted manuscripts that pass peer review in ostensibly legitimate journals, shows that volume-based incentives corrupt the research record even when every formal quality marker is present. Reading the Philippine case alongside this global pattern suggests that whitelisting indexed venues is necessary but insufficient. Accountability requires Philippine authorities to complement indexing criteria with a national research integrity framework, institutional verification of authorship, conference, and data provenance, and financial support that does not make ethical publishing contingent on personal wealth.

articles_hidden.title: Unequal Geographic Coverage of Air-Quality Monitoring across Wealth Groups in Delhi
articles_hidden.authors: Saishha Vikram Agarwal
articles_hidden.abstract: Air-quality monitoring networks are the basis for measuring and reporting urban pollution, but their value depends in part on how well they represent the populations they are intended to serve. The study examines whether Delhi's air-quality monitoring network provides equal geographic coverage across wealth groups. It combines the locations of current air-quality monitoring stations with the Relative Wealth Index (RWI), which provides estimates of relative wealth for small geographic areas. Delhi's population is divided into five population-weighted wealth groups, and the distance from each location to the nearest monitor is calculated. Residents in the poorest wealth quintile live, on average, 7.58 km from the nearest monitor, compared with 4.69 km for the richest quintile. The difference of 2.89 km is positive even after accounting for spatial clustering (95% spatial-block bootstrap interval: 1.60 to 4.28 km). Monitoring coverage is also higher among the highest-wealth residents: 45.7% of the poorest quintile lives within 5 km of a monitor compared with 67.3% of the richest quintile. The results show that Delhi's monitoring network provides unequal geographic coverage across wealth groups. The study contributes theoretically by framing monitoring-network representativeness as an equity question. Practically, it contributes by suggesting that future network expansion consider population-weighted accessibility and coverage of lower-wealth populations along with conventional technical siting criteria. The results do not, however, show that monitors were deliberately placed to favor wealthier areas, nor do they establish that greater distance necessarily causes less accurate pollution measurement.

articles_hidden.title: An Overview of Public Administration Research: Insights From Publications in Leading Journals (2000–2024)
articles_hidden.authors: Vener Garayev
articles_hidden.abstract: This study examines paradigmatic changes, thematic developments and authorship patterns in public administration research by analyzing 4,317 articles published in Public Administration Review, Public Management Review, and Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory between 2000 and 2024. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques through Python software to analyze content of titles, abstracts, and metadata, the article identifies key thematic clusters and paradigmatic shifts across the period, shaped by global events, contextual challenges, and technological advancements. The findings reveal a transition from bureaucratic efficiency to participatory governance, from reform to resilience, and from administrative theory to data-driven governance. Additionally, analysis of authorship patterns reveals increasing collaboration and concentration of scholarly output among top prolific contributors. This study contributes to a growing body of literature on bibliometric and content analytical studies in public administration, offering a comprehensive, data-driven perspective on the field’s intellectual evolution over the past quarter-century.

articles_hidden.title: Apuestas en Chile: regulación y peso económico de un mercado en expansión
articles_hidden.authors: Andrés Araya; Fabian Belmar; Xiomara Kuwae; Sebastián Aliaga
articles_hidden.abstract: El mercado de apuestas ya no puede entenderse solo como una actividad presencial. La expansión de internet, los teléfonos inteligentes, los medios de pago digitales y la publicidad deportiva trasladó parte relevante del juego de azar hacia plataformas online. Chile reguló históricamente el juego mediante autorizaciones parciales: hípica, loterías, casinos municipales y casinos bajo la Ley N.º 19.995. Ese diseño permitió ordenar segmentos específicos, pero quedó tensionado frente a un mercado digital transnacional. El juego de azar es un problema de política pública, no solo una actividad recreativa. Involucra recaudación fiscal, competencia entre operadores, protección al consumidor, prevención de lavado de activos, integridad deportiva y riesgos asociados al juego problemático. El mercado online no autorizado se ubica en una zona compleja: no forma parte del mercado autorizado, pero tampoco ha sido desplazado de manera efectiva. La Corte Suprema ha declarado ilegales las apuestas online no autorizadas, mientras persisten dificultades prácticas de fiscalización, persecución penal y control de dominios. En 2025, el mercado regulado registró ingresos brutos del juego por $787.281 millones (0,23% del PIB) y generó $148.712 millones en recaudación específica asociada al juego de azar, sin considerar IVA ni impuesto a la renta. Cerca del 70% del mercado regulado corresponde a casinos físicos. Este informe estima el mercado online no autorizado como la brecha entre la tendencia contrafactual del mercado regulado y sus ingresos efectivamente observados. En 2025, esa brecha alcanzó $431.489 millones (0,13% del PIB), es decir, poco más de un tercio de la industria. Bajo una tasa específica de 20% sobre ingresos brutos del juego, la pérdida potencial de recaudación sectorial asociada al mercado online no autorizado se aproxima a $86.298 millones en 2025.

articles_hidden.title: Crecer en campamentos. El drama de un doble vínculo
articles_hidden.authors: Rosario Palacios; Fabian Belmar; Aldo Mascareño
articles_hidden.abstract: En la última década, los campamentos en Chile se han vuelto, nuevamente, una alternativa de habitación permanente para familias de bajos ingresos, sin capacidad de ahorro o inmigrantes. Su número ha pasado de cerca de 700 campamentos en 2011 a alrededor de 1.400 en 2025, en los que viven cerca de 120.000 familias y 84.000 niños. Por medio de análisis estadísticos de tres bases de datos construidas a partir de cuestionarios a cuidadores de niños en campamentos de cinco regiones del país, en este artículo argumentamos que la vida en campamentos produce para los niños un doble vínculo: por un lado, los expone a altos riesgos de entorno, seguridad y económicos, pero la permanencia en el campamento estabiliza su inclusión educativa y de salud, además de hacerlos visibles para beneficios sociales. Los resultados confirman este patrón dual en variables relevantes y, a la vez, abren una posibilidad de superación de esta condición a través de los llamados barrios transitorios, unidades reguladas factualmente (territorio cercado, en márgenes de campamento), socialmente (reglamento comunitario, selección) y temporalmente (orientación a vivienda definitiva). Estos barrios erigen barreras de inmunidad que mantienen la inclusión institucional de los niños (educación, salud, beneficios) y, a la vez, reducen significativamente sus riesgos de entorno, de seguridad y económicos. El artículo concluye que el modelo de barrios transitorios tiene potencial para convertirse en una política público-privada de salida de campamentos hacia soluciones de vivienda definitivas, aunque con limitaciones en cuanto a tiempos y envergadura.

articles_hidden.title: El lado B de la megarreforma: señales de alerta temprana sobre problemas futuros
articles_hidden.authors: Aldo Mascareño; Fabian Belmar; Pablo A. Henríquez; Juan Rozas
articles_hidden.abstract: Desde el anuncio del Proyecto de Reconstrucción la discusión pública ha girado en torno a temáticas económicas organizadas por la diferencia entre crecimiento y estabilidad fiscal. El predominio de estos temas tiene el efecto de eclipsar otros problemas sociales —emergentes o derivados del proyecto de reconstrucción— que se incuban en las capas subyacentes de esta discusión. Por medio de un análisis computacional de datos de redes sociales, en este artículo argumentamos que tales problemas incuban situaciones críticas futuras que pueden transformarse en conflictos mayores en el mediano plazo. Para ello extraemos las weak signals (señales débiles de alerta temprana) que anuncian procesos de incubación de problemas complejos. Los resultados muestran que estas situaciones críticas se forman en diversos ámbitos que van desde la seguridad hasta la cultura, pasando por problemas sociales clásicos, medioambientales, de género y tecnológicos. El artículo concluye que el análisis de señales débiles, o señales de alerta temprana, ofrece oportunidades de intervención antes de que los problemas se hagan ingobernables, por lo que muestra su utilidad cuando el interventor tiene capacidad de acción y decisión para desactivar constelaciones críticas emergentes.

articles_hidden.title: La cuenta pública del presidente Kast: una cuestión doctrinaria
articles_hidden.authors: Aldo Mascareño; Juan Rozas; Pablo A. Henríquez; Fabian Belmar
articles_hidden.abstract: Las primeras cuentas públicas de cada presidente reflejan su diagnóstico de la situación del país y el sentido programático que le quieren imprimir a su gobierno. Las capacidades de articulación entre los problemas de las personas y una visión de sociedad de largo plazo anclada en principios doctrinarios que orientan la acción política son clave en este tipo de discursos. Por medio de distintos procedimientos algorítmicos de análisis de texto, en este artículo argumentamos que la primera cuenta pública del presidente José Antonio Kast muestra selecciones temáticas y lingüísticas que evidencian un sentido doctrinario distinto al expresado por otros gobiernos chilenos desde el retorno a la democracia en 1990. Los resultados muestran que hay varias condiciones de continuidad en los pesos programáticos del discurso del presidente Kast en comparación con la primera cuenta de los presidentes anteriores, por ejemplo, en temas políticos y económicos. Sin embargo, una diferencia radical está en el posicionamiento inédito, en el primer lugar, del tema de seguridad, lo que anticipa un conjunto de reformas institucionales y discursivas profundas. Los resultados también muestran que la construcción doctrinaria de este primer discurso se articula sobre los conceptos de familia, patria y esfuerzo, los que funcionan como nodos de legitimación y justificación de las acciones políticas propuestas. El artículo concluye que el discurso inaugura un nuevo escenario político que se alinea no solo con la eficacia de las políticas, sino con el tipo de sociedad que impulsan.

articles_hidden.title: What QCA Cannot See: Identification Bounds for Configurational Solutions with Missing Set Memberships
articles_hidden.authors: Maikel Yelandi Leyva Vázquez
articles_hidden.abstract: Qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) needs a membership score for every case in every set, and applied studies commonly remove cases whose scores are missing. In a truth table, removal can turn a configuration that exists but was not scored into a logical remainder available as a simplifying assumption. We propose partial-identification QCA (PI-QCA). Each missing score is represented by an interval, every completion is considered, and the analysis reports exact bounds for the consistency and coverage of any term, the sure solution (the terms present in the solution of every completion), the possible region, bracketed by an inner bound from sampled completions and an outer bound from enumeration, and the identification gap. A solution outside the outer bound is produced by no completion. By construction, the sure solution cannot contain a term absent from the complete-data solution. In 900 simulated data sets its sampled approximation also satisfied this in every replicate, whereas case deletion and mean imputation returned false terms about as often as the complete-data analysis on average but up to 22 percentage points more often under some missingness mechanisms. The price is an empty sure solution in 71–95% of replicates when a fifth of the scores were missing. In an illustration with 131 economies, deletion returns a solution that no completion produces when the outcome is kept at its recorded values. Reanalyses of two published studies find a certified empty sure solution for one outcome and, for another, published solutions attained by none of 208 sampled completions.

articles_hidden.title: A Step, Not a Slope: The Global Rise of Anti-Government Protest, 1990–2025
articles_hidden.authors: Sanmit Tanmay Ratnaparkhi
articles_hidden.abstract: Analysts have described the 2010s as an era of mass protest and expect protests to continue to increase. How did the frequency of antigovernmental protests change globally from 1990 to 2019? And what does the pattern imply for the years ahead? This is the question of the study. We used linear regression with annual counts of protests from the Mass Mobilization dataset (15,143 protests in 168 countries, 147–160 in any one year). The data was well fit by a simple linear trend (adding around 12 protests a year), but the fit was much better with a model that included a one-time shift in 2011: protests jumped by around 244 events per year after 2011, with little or no year-on-year trend. The break in 2011 was detected independently by a structural break test. After controlling for world population growth, the step remained significant. ACLED data for the period 2021-2025 did not show a significant further increase in the global total, although protests rose sharply in some countries and fell in others. Armed rebellion was not counted, so falling protest numbers may partly reflect a change in the form of dissent rather than a decline in dissent itself, as in Myanmar after 2021, where dissent became armed resistance. So global protest seems to have reached a new, higher plateau rather than to be on a steady upward climb, warning against linear projections of ever-increasing dissent.

articles_hidden.title: Demographer Views about U.S. Fertility: Results from a Survey
articles_hidden.authors: Philip N. Cohen
articles_hidden.abstract: The view that birth rates in the U.S. (where the total fertility rate is now 1.57) is a crisis – even an existential crisis – is increasingly common, but academic demography has not adopted this frame. Demographers should not expect unquestioning acceptance of our views on population issues, but it is useful to make our perspective known, individually as well as collectively. To that end, I report on a new survey of 190 self-identified U.S. demographic researchers (either U.S. nationals or based in the U.S.) on birth rates and population trends. The sample was drawn from demography journal authors, with a response rate of 27.7%. Results show that only 3% agreed the U.S. is in a “demographic crisis.” A majority agreed that government should take measures in order to increase fertility if the total fertility rate were to fall to 0.8 – while 43% believe governments should “never intervene” to raise birth rates. On the other hand, with “the right policies,” 84% agreed the U.S. would benefit from substantially increased immigration. Asked to rank global population issues for the coming years, respondents ranked climate change, aging, and inequality most important, with low birth rates rating eighth out of 12 issues.

articles_hidden.title: 2000년~2025년 출생아 수 변화의 인구학적 요인 분해분석과 최근 반등에 대한 함의(Demographic Decomposition of Changes in the Number of Births in Korea, 2000–2025: Implications for the Recent Rebound)
articles_hidden.authors: Changin Jeon
articles_hidden.abstract:
본 연구는 2000~2025년 한국의 출생아 수 변화를 여성인구, 유배우 비율, 유배우 출산율, 무배우 출산율의 네 요인으로 완전분해하고, 각 요인의 기여를 다시 두 성분으로 나눈다. 곧 곡선 전체가 공통으로 오르내린 몫인 수준 성분과, 전체 수준은 그대로인 채 연령 간 비중이 옮겨간 몫인 연령패턴 성분이다. 이 성분 분해는 기존 출생아 수 정의식에 기초한 것이므로 성분별 기여의 합이 요인 기여와 정확히 일치하며, 완결출산력의 참값을 미리 지정한 시뮬레이션으로 성분 구성의 판정 기준을 마련하였다. 분석 결과, 유배우 출산율 효과는 장기적으로 출생아 수를 늘리는 방향이었지만, 이는 출산이 30대로 집중되면서 곡선 전체의 수준 하락을 상쇄하고도 남은 결과였다. 순효과만 보면 유배우 출산력이 상승한 듯하지만 성분을 나누면 오히려 수준이 하락했음이 드러난다. 시뮬레이션에서 완결출산력의 변화 없이 혼인만 지연되면 특정 연령대로 출산이 몰린 성분이 수준 성분을 앞서는 반면, 완결출산력이 실제로 상승할 때에는 수준 성분이 주도한다. 이 기준으로 보면 2005~2012년 회복기는 실제 출산력 상승에 부합하지만, 2023~2025년 최근 반등은 혼인 지연에 따른 결과에 더 가깝다. 본 연구는 최근의 출생아 수 반등이 어떤 성격을 갖고 있는지 판정할 수 있는 기준을 마련하는데 의의가 있다.

This study decomposes changes in the number of births in Korea between 2000 and 2025 into four factors (the female population, the proportion of married women, marital fertility, and non-marital fertility) and further divides each factor's contribution into two components: a level component, the share attributable to the curve as a whole moving up or down uniformly, and an age-pattern component, the share attributable to relative weights shifting across ages while the overall level remains unchanged. Because this component decomposition is simply a rewriting of the identity defining the number of births, the components sum exactly to the factor contributions. Reference criteria for interpreting the component composition were established through a simulation in which the true value of completed marital fertility is specified in advance. The results show that the marital fertility effect worked to raise the number of births over the long run, but only because the concentration of childbearing into the thirties more than offset a decline in the level of the curve as a whole. Judged by the net effect alone, marital fertility appears to have risen; once the components are separated, it becomes evident that the level in fact declined. In the simulation, when marriage is postponed with no change in completed fertility, the component reflecting the concentration of births into particular ages outweighs the level component, whereas when completed fertility genuinely rises, the level component predominates. By this criterion, the 2005–2012 recovery is consistent with a genuine rise in fertility, whereas the recent rebound of 2023–2025 is closer to a consequence of marriage postponement. This study provides criteria for determining the nature of the recent rebound.

articles_hidden.title: Mistrust the State, Trust the Market  Mass Investing Culture with Postsocialist Flavour
articles_hidden.authors: Karel Němeček
articles_hidden.abstract: In this paper, I aim to make sense of the meanings surrounding the recent surge in popularity of non-professional investing in the Czech and Slovak postsocialist context. The research is based on interviews with individual retail investors and fieldwork conducted at various investor events, meet-ups, and conferences. My Czech and Slovak research partners view investing as a means to ensure the long-term continuation of their household’s wealth and security. Being invested then represents a certain hedge against the growing inaccessibility of housing and the cost-of-living crisis. My interviewees entrust what Giddens calls ontological security to institutions of global capitalism rather than to local state systems. The shift in trust remains embedded in distinctly postsocialist moral framing, proclaiming a more ethical, self-responsible, and rational type of household financial management, which aligns with the core moral imperative of mass investment culture – everybody should invest. Conversely, welfare-state-based alternatives face generalized distrust as unreliable.

articles_hidden.title: Building better parenting leave survey data: A repository of survey questions for comparative policy analysis
articles_hidden.authors: Cassandra Engeman; Marie Valentova; Laurène Thil; Anna Stastna; Anne Hartung; Alzbeta Bartova; Ivana Dobrotic; Ásdís A. Arnalds; Stephan Köppe; Elitsa Dimitrova
articles_hidden.abstract: This document presents a repository of questions that can be used in cross-national comparative surveys to collect data on parenting leave. With our collated and proposed questions, we aim to assist researchers and data collection agencies build better parenting leave data to understand when and how parents use such provisions. In the following sections, we present questions related to measuring (1) formal and perceived eligibility for leave provisions, (2) leave use and non-use, (3) reasons for non-use, and (4) views about parenting leave. While questions in the first three sections primarily measure behaviour, we include questions about parents’ views, because they can inform behaviour. Each of these four main sections includes our research- and theory-based motivations for the phrasing, inclusion and design of the questions as well as their shortcomings.

articles_hidden.title: Ecological responsibility, wellbeing, and transformative reach: a three-dimensional framework for assessing ecovillages as social innovations toward sustainability
articles_hidden.authors: Alexandre Zénon
articles_hidden.abstract: Ecovillages are collective experiments in maintaining wellbeing within planetary limits, testing whether human flourishing can be maintained while material throughput is reduced. Drawing on a critical narrative review of intentional communities, ecological economics, commons governance, and self-determination theory, we propose a three- dimension, two-layer framework joining ecological limits, wellbeing, and the propagation dynamics of social innovations. The outcome layer includes five elements across three dimensions: critical natural capital and biophysical flows (ecological), material sufficiency and eudaimonic wellbeing (wellbeing), and transformative effect (transformative), an outward axis specific to social innovations. The lever layer includes three transversal levers: a sufficiency economy that drives throughput reduction, a commons governance built on Ostrom's design principles, and a propagation infrastructure that carries practices beyond the host site. Empirically, ecovillages deliver 35 to 80% footprint reductions and achieve partial closure of nutrient cycles. They meet a decent material floor through commons-based provisioning while sustaining or improving wellbeing. They propagate practices via transmission, replication, partnerships, and political influence. Four structural challenges constrain systemic contribution: limited actual impact on ecological, host- territory, and cultural dimensions; dependence on the mainstream provisioning system; barriers to scale (demanding resident profiles, high attrition); and social selection. We argue that ecovillages are best understood as generative laboratories of transposable knowledge and living alternatives that act as vectors of cultural changes. We propose an agenda for a wider community-based transition, associating multi-scale architectures with supportive economic models, facilitative institutions, and a deliberate research program. We situate this Northern articulation within a wider pluriverse of place-based sustainability projects, of which ecovillages are one strand among many.

articles_hidden.title: The Evolutionary Hearth: An Environment-Dependent Game-Theoretic Framework for Javanese Maternal Domestic Pedagogy
articles_hidden.authors: Muhammad Sukri Bin Ramli
articles_hidden.abstract: This study introduces the Principle of Conditional Cultural Adaptiveness, establishing that the evolutionary performance of cultural strategies depends strictly on environmental state variables and shifts through equilibrium migration as those macro-conditions change. Modernity is formally conceptualized not as cultural erosion, but as equilibrium migration between state-dependent optima. Existing scholarly interpretations of Javanese maternal domesticity and the construct of kanca wingking frequently emphasize patriarchal gender hierarchies, symbolic cosmology, or moral norms without formally modeling how domestic practices dynamically adjust to resource volatility, environmental hazards, and shifting household bargaining power. We develop an environment-dependent game-theoretic frame work linking selected maternal instructions to material resource allocation, homeostatic regulation, risk management, health capital investment, cultural information transmission, and costly signaling. By integrating ethnographic philology with evolutionary game theory, bargaining theory, dynamic optimization, and eco-evolutionary feedback modeling, this research provides a formal computational social science framework for representing cultural persistence and transformation while explicitly differentiating stable household equilibria from equitable distributions of welfare.

articles_hidden.title: Polity Size and Women's Representation: Evidence from Two Large-scale Boundary Reforms
articles_hidden.authors: Moa Frödin-Gruneau; Jan Teorell; Kåre Vernby
articles_hidden.abstract: Do larger polities hinder gender parity in elected office? We theorize that when populations grow faster than elected assemblies, a “seat congestion” effect intensifies competition for nominations, enabling men candidates to crowd out women. We test this argument using two nationwide natural experiments: Swedish municipal amalgamations in 1952 and 1973 that abruptly increased electorates. We track the effects in newly digitized historical panel data. Where electorate-per-seat ratios rose, growth in women's representation slowed. Decomposition analyses show that expanding councils only partially offsets congestion. By identifying polity size as a systematic brake on descriptive representation, the study adds a demographic dimension to debates on institutional design and points to an overlooked cost of increasing jurisdictional size.

articles_hidden.title: Organicity And Structural Coincidence. Intellectual Activity Across Fields
articles_hidden.authors: Matteo Puoti; Antoine Roger
articles_hidden.abstract:
Intellectual activity is examined as a crucial component in the formation of dominant principles of perception, classification, and action. Drawing on Bourdieu’s field theory, the analysis focuses on the structural coincidence of struggles across relatively autonomous fields, showing how concordant principles may emerge without central coordination and contribute to naturalising the established order. Gramsci’s concepts of organicity, intellectual function, civil society, and common sense broaden this perspective by extending the range of agents, practices, and institutions implicated in hegemonic processes. This also foregrounds their relational and pedagogical dimensions and the need for an empirical inventory of the sites and symbolic forms through which common sense takes shape. Hegemony is thus treated as the contingent outcome of differentiated struggles whose effects become aligned across fields. A case study of agricultural capitalism in Romania illustrates the empirical operationalisation of this framework.

For a fuller discussion and further developments of these themes:
https://www.routledge.com/On-Gramsci-and-Bourdieu-Hegemony-Fields-and-Tools-for-Social-Research/Puoti-Roger/p/book/9781041299523
